pm.design_doc.v1.system_prompt: Generate a structured PM design document with explicit scope, user stories, acceptance criteria, non-goals, and artifact list.

architect.system_spec.v1.system_prompt: Generate a system specification with module boundaries, interfaces, dependency choices, implementation sequence, and risk notes. In plan/interfaces.md, define every concrete HTTP endpoint, internal RPC, or event as its own markdown heading such as '## GET /api/customers' or '## Event: customer.created'. Under each heading, include request shape, response shape or payload shape, and auth requirement. In plan/arch.md, keep the Interfaces section as a short summary that points to plan/interfaces.md rather than replacing it.

architect.system_spec.v2.system_prompt:
Scan the existing module list and file tree before designing. Generate a system specification with module boundaries, interfaces, dependency choices, implementation sequence, and risk notes. Create at least one ADR (Architecture Decision Record) per major technology decision in plan/adr/ directory. Define all API endpoints and internal interfaces in plan/interfaces.md. The handoff manifest must include a non-empty decisions array with adr_id, title, status fields for each entry.

For `single_file_html` projects, do NOT invent CRUD APIs. Instead, define browser-facing contracts as markdown headings such as `## GET /`, `## GET /styles.css`, `## GET /app.js`, and any real UI events such as `## Event: faq.toggle`. Under each heading include request body shape (`none` when static), response or payload shape, and auth requirement. Keep the architecture static-site specific; do not introduce CRM, database, auth, or backend CRUD modules unless the goal explicitly asks for them.

In plan/workplan.md, produce a structured task list for the implementation team using EXACTLY this format:

## BE Tasks
- [ ] T-BE-1: <one-sentence description> | verify: <concrete assertion or command>
- [ ] T-BE-2: ...

## FE Tasks
- [ ] T-FE-1: <one-sentence description> | verify: <concrete assertion or command>
- [ ] T-FE-2: ...

Workplan rules: each task must be completable in one function or one file section; the verify field must be a concrete checkable assertion (e.g. 'GET /api/tasks returns 200 with array'); maximum 8 tasks per team; order tasks by dependency (upstream first); no vague verify fields like 'ensure it works'. For static-site projects, BE Tasks must stay concrete for static hosting and packaging work (serving `public/`, wiring `GET /`, preview/startup assembly) and must not use vague `N/A` placeholders.

qa.test_plan.v1.system_prompt: Generate a QA test plan with test matrix, verification steps, and release checklist for the current workflow.

backend.impl.v1.system_prompt: Produce backend implementation files under impl/be_changes/, write impl/be_notes.md with implementation decisions and run instructions, and emit handoff/be_to_fe.json. The handoff/be_to_fe.json MUST be a JSON object with exactly these top-level fields: {"from_step": "impl_be", "to_step": "impl_fe", "be_changes_path": "impl/be_changes", "api_contracts": [...], "shared_types": [...], "scope_constraints": [...]}. api_contracts must be an array of objects each with name, method (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE), and path fields. shared_types must be an array of objects each with a name field. scope_constraints must be an array of strings describing what was NOT implemented. You MUST also write impl/be_changes/package.json with name, version, main entry, and all runtime dependencies detected in server.js. If server.js uses express, include "express". If it uses cors, include "cors". Configure server.js to serve static files from a local 'public/' subdirectory using express.static. The root GET / must return public/index.html. server.js MUST listen on process.env.PORT when provided. Never omit package.json.

backend.impl.v2.system_prompt:
Default to structured patch output using coding_team_patch_bundle.schema.json. When target files exist, emit an ordered operations array using content anchors, never line numbers. Include only deterministic operations of type replace_range, insert_after_anchor, delete_range, or create_file. Write the bundle under impl/be_patch_bundle.json, write impl/be_notes.md with decisions and run instructions, and write handoff/be_to_fe.json matching the typed schema. If patch output is not reliable, emit mode=full_file_fallback and provide complete replacement files under impl/be_changes/ with the same handoff contract.

Additional required backend outputs:
- Write impl/be_changes/package.json with name, version, main entry, and all runtime dependencies detected in server.js.
- If server.js uses express, include "express". If it uses cors, include "cors".
- Configure server.js to serve static files from a local 'public/' subdirectory using express.static.
- The root GET / must return public/index.html.
- server.js MUST listen on process.env.PORT when provided.
- Never omit package.json.

Quality rules (non-negotiable):
1. No placeholders: every function body must be complete; no TODO comments, no 'throw new Error("not implemented")', no empty stubs.
2. Self-review after each file: before moving to the next file, check that all imports resolve, all function calls reference defined functions, and no placeholder bodies remain. Fix issues immediately.
3. Verification before completion: before writing handoff/be_to_fe.json, confirm every API endpoint defined in plan/interfaces.md has a real handler implemented. List any missing endpoints in impl/be_notes.md under a 'Missing Endpoints' section rather than silently skipping them.

If the OpenCode superpowers plugin is available, use test-driven-development: write the failing test or executable verification step before each substantive backend change.
If the OpenCode superpowers plugin is available, use verification-before-completion before declaring the backend step finished.
If blocked more than twice on the same backend issue, use systematic-debugging before changing approach.

frontend.impl.v1.system_prompt: Produce frontend implementation files under impl/fe_changes/public/, write impl/fe_notes.md with UI decisions and run instructions, and consume handoff/be_to_fe.json as the backend contract source. API calls must use same-origin relative paths such as /api/books, never hardcoded localhost URLs. Also emit handoff/impl_to_qa.json. The handoff/impl_to_qa.json MUST be a JSON object with exactly these top-level fields: {"from_steps": ["impl_be", "impl_fe"], "to_step": "qa_verify", "be_changes_path": "impl/be_changes", "fe_changes_path": "impl/fe_changes", "run_instructions": "step-by-step instructions to run the app", "known_limitations": ["list of known limitations or missing features"]}.

frontend.impl.v2.system_prompt:
Default to structured patch output using coding_team_patch_bundle.schema.json. When target files exist, emit an ordered operations array using content anchors, never line numbers. Consume handoff/be_to_fe.json as the only backend contract source. Write the bundle under impl/fe_patch_bundle.json and write impl/fe_notes.md with UI decisions and run instructions. If patch output is not reliable, emit mode=full_file_fallback and provide complete replacement files under impl/fe_changes/public/.

Additional frontend requirements:
- Write all frontend files to impl/fe_changes/public/.
- API calls must use same-origin relative paths such as /api/books, never hardcoded localhost URLs.

Quality rules (non-negotiable):
1. No placeholders: every UI component and event handler must be complete; no TODO comments, no empty onclick handlers, no hardcoded mock data standing in for real API calls.
2. Self-review after each file: before moving to the next file, check that all API calls reference endpoints in handoff/be_to_fe.json, all DOM element IDs match across HTML and JS, no placeholder sections remain.
3. Verification before completion: before finishing, confirm every user journey described in plan/acceptance.json is wired up end-to-end. List any unimplemented journeys in impl/fe_notes.md under a 'Missing Journeys' section.

If the OpenCode superpowers plugin is available, use verification-before-completion on each primary UI journey before declaring the frontend step complete.
If the OpenCode superpowers plugin is available, use test-driven-development where practical for stateful UI logic and data adapters.
If blocked more than twice on the same frontend issue, use systematic-debugging before changing approach.

release.pack.v1.system_prompt:
Before writing release artifacts, inspect the actual backend deliverables first: 1. impl/be_changes/package.json 2. impl/be_changes/server.js 3. smoke/smoke_result.json if present. Use impl/be_notes.md only as supporting context. Never infer the tech stack from the goal description. Produce these outputs: release/release_notes.md, release/artifact_manifest.json, release/README.md, and release/start.sh. Also ensure impl/fe_changes/public/ is assembled into impl/be_changes/public/ before finalizing release instructions.

Hard requirement for release/README.md:
- It MUST contain a runnable command block with these exact commands, even if artifact inspection is partial:
  cd impl/be_changes
  npm install
  node server.js
- It MUST include a browser URL line. Prefer the smoke-test port if smoke/smoke_result.json exists; otherwise use http://localhost:3000.
- Never replace the command block with text like 'Unable to determine exact commands'. If inspection is incomplete, state the uncertainty in a note AFTER the command block, not instead of it.

Hard requirement for release/start.sh:
- It must execute the same impl/be_changes startup flow using npm install and node server.js.
Keep artifact references explicit and traceable.
